Messages.Author: rai...@mich.com
Messages.Body:
The Corruption card says "Put a corruption counter on a vampire or ally
controlled by your prey. If the number of your corruption counters on
the minion equals or exceeds the blood capacity of that vampire or the
cost of that ally, you may burn all of your corruption counters on that
minion to gain control of him or her."

My question is once the Corruption action has been taken, are further
corruption cards required to add corruption counters to the corrupt
minion.

A question to WoTC came back stating "With corruption, you would need
five corruption cards to take five directed actions, putting five
corruption counters on a five blood vampire to take control of that
vampire."

I have tried using the corruption cards in this fashion and found that
to have any effect on your prey, you need to have 1/3 of your deck filled
with these cards. If the corruption was placed and then further action,
without cards were taken to corrupt a vampire (without +1 stealth), a deck
does not have to be completely filled with corruption cards.

Having 30 corruption cards in a deck ruins the deck for anything else,
and anything else make the likelyhood of corruption a vampire remote.
Unless your prey has a weinie vote deck.

So how should this card really work?

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
rai...@mich.com wrote:
>
> The Corruption card says "Put a corruption counter on a vampire or ally
> controlled by your prey. If the number of your corruption counters on
> the minion equals or exceeds the blood capacity of that vampire or the
> cost of that ally, you may burn all of your corruption counters on that
> minion to gain control of him or her."
>
> My question is once the Corruption action has been taken, are further
> corruption cards required to add corruption counters to the corrupt
> minion.

Yes. (Or, you could use any other effect which placed Corruption
counters. There are no other such effects currently, but some future
expansion might include some.)

> A question to WoTC came back stating "With corruption, you would need
> five corruption cards to take five directed actions, putting five
> corruption counters on a five blood vampire to take control of that
> vampire."

This is correct, unless you have some way of re-using your corruption
cards (Carlotta or Whispers from the Dead).

> I have tried using the corruption cards in this fashion and found that
> to have any effect on your prey, you need to have 1/3 of your deck filled
> with these cards. If the corruption was placed and then further action,
> without cards were taken to corrupt a vampire (without +1 stealth), a deck
> does not have to be completely filled with corruption cards.

True, you would need fewer Corruption cards if the Corruption card
was placed on the target an allowed a cardless action to add more
Corruption counters. But its does not.

> Having 30 corruption cards in a deck ruins the deck for anything else,
> and anything else make the likelyhood of corruption a vampire remote.
> Unless your prey has a weinie vote deck.
>
> So how should this card really work?

You've got it.
If you can't spare the 30 slots in your deck, just use five or
eight and use the Corruptions to steal Allies that cost only a
few pool. Then, if you find yourself in position to steal a
young vampire from a voting deck, so much the better.

--
L. Scott Johnson (vte...@regency.wizards.com)

I actually just recently used Corruption to good effect in my
Giovanni/Settite
deck. (Giovanni/Settite Deck? Yes. Kherebetu was too nifty for anything
less.)
Managed to use Carlotta Giovanni to recycle through the Corruption cards
and
take control of an 8 capacity vampire. Meanwhile, my opponent's resources
were dedicated heavily to stopping the whole thing, which left me time to
build up. (I had the Edge.) I could have won the game without it, but it
was a nifty coup.

It's also great against tiny allies. No better way to hose Ambrosius with
Talbot's Chainsaw than to steal him.

Don't make such a brutal effort to corrupt. Corruption is subtle.
Use it only for the kid-vamps of your prey, or allies. I play in a
group with a 5 card limit, and use the card as a surprise effect.
I have all 5 cards allowed in my deck and play them to get the Caitiff
who diablerizes this evil big vamp of my predator, to take my
advantage of 3rd Traditions or Embraces and "normal" Allies like Arcanum
Investigator. Possible is also to first play "Mark of Damnation" on a
small famed Vampire of your prey (he will smile), corrupt him (his smile
will freeze) and send him in a rampaging frenzy to destroy this art
museum... :)
Or, someone posted it, play with Carlotta Giovanni. She will recycle the
Corruption cards for you. Let Kimintiri first bury her "Heart of
Darkness" and then snip off her "Ruthor's Hand" to get along with the
actions you need. Kherebutu may copy Carlotta if he listens the
"Whispers from the Dead" (pretty expensive, better use Dedefra).

If you have access to the more esoteric Setite cards like "Form of
Corruption" or "Temptation", use them. (both rare)

All in all, Corruption is a nice card, but not decisive. It is only a
stone in the wall, but a pretty one.

Michael Beer, Dortmund, Germany
